sentences.text: The petitioner, whose properties were acquired for the purpose of "Vizhinjam International Seaport", alleges that, while the compensation eligible to him was disbursed, the value of a Well in the acquired property had not been reckoned.

He says that he, therefore, preferred Ext.P12 application before the District Collector, which has, however, been rejected through Ext.P13 citing,
inter alia, that the Well in question was constructed in the year 2011, as admitted by him, which is much after the preliminary notification for acquisition had been issued.
2. Sri.

N.S.Gopakumar - learned counsel for the petitioner, vehemently argued that the reasons stated in Ext.P13, to reject his client's Ext.P12 request, are untenable because, he came to be aware that the Well had been acquired only in 2022; and for the second, the Well was actually constructed in the year 2004 and not in 2011, as now found by the District Collector.
He thus prayed that Ext.P13 be set aside and Ext.P12 be directed to be reconsidered by the District Collector.

3. However, in response, Smt.Merlyn Mathew - learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent,
submitted that the afore assertions of the petitioner are untrue because, the property was acquired from him under a negotiated settlement, being thus fully aware of the attributes of the property.

She then added that, whatever the petitioner may now say, he himself admits that he has sworn to an affidavit before the 5 th respondent to the effect that the Well was constructed in the year 2011 and hence that payment of compensation against it is impermissible because the preliminary notification of acquisition was issued as early as on 29.07.2010.
She thus prayed that this Writ Petition be dismissed.

4. Sri.Riyal Devassy - learned Government Pleader, adopted the afore submissions of Smt.Merlyn Mathew, however, adding that once compensation was accepted by the petitioner voluntarily under a Direct Purchase Agreement, any further escalation is impossible; and that, in any event, the value of the Well cannot be now sought for after a decade, particularly when the acquisition process had been completed much earlier.

sentences.text: I must say upfront that the afore submissions of Smt.Merlyn Mathew and Sri.Riyal Devassy appeal to this Court.

This is because, the question whether the Well was constructed in the year 2004 or 2011 are aspects in the factual realm, into which, this Court cannot enter while acting under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

Furthermore, the petitioner himself admits, in paragraph 8 of memorandum of the Writ Petition that he had sworn to an affidavit averring that the Well was constructed in the year 2011, but now asserts that it was on account of 'oversight' and as instructed by the 5 th respondent.

These aspects cannot be evaluated by this Court on its merits and the petitioner will have to invoke other remedies, including under the Civil Law, as may be available,
subject to laws of limitation.

In the afore circumstances, without entering into the merits of any of the rival contentions, I close this Writ Petition; however, leaving full liberty to the petitioner to invoke any other remedy as may be available to him.
